observation.visible_scene: An outdoor ground-level campfire built inside a rough ring of mossy rocks on a dirt, leaf-strewn clearing, with a tree trunk and the legs of a wooden bench in the background. A small pile of twigs burns in the center with orange-yellow flames. A person's hand and forearm enter from the left edge of the frame holding a thin twig/stick.
visible_changes: The flames flicker and continuously change height and shape throughout the whole excerpt (taller and more spread in some frames, e.g. 1, 35-40; lower and narrower in others), consistent with ongoing combustion.
From about frame 8 to frame 16 the hand extends the thin stick rightward so its tip reaches into the burning pile, holding it there while the fire burns around it.
From frame 17 onward the hand opens, the stick is no longer held out, and the hand retreats leftward, leaving the frame entirely by roughly frame 26.
After the hand exits (frames 27-41) only the fire remains, still flickering; the surrounding rocks, ground, tree and bench legs do not move, indicating a static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the person did with the stick after releasing it (whether it was added to the fire, removed from view, or dropped) is not visible.
The state of the fire before the clip and its eventual outcome are outside the excerpt.
The identity or body of the person is unseen beyond the hand/forearm.
uncertain_details: Whether the stick was placed into the fire or simply withdrawn is ambiguous; it disappears from the hand between frames 16 and 17 without a clearly visible transfer.
The exact frame at which the hand fully leaves the left edge is approximate due to sampling.
